title: The WHO Constitution's definition of health
body: The Constitution of the World Health Organization states a definition that the WHO still quotes as a guiding principle: "Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity." The same statement of principles says the enjoyment of the highest attainable standard of health is a fundamental right of every human being without distinction of race. The definition is broader than "not sick." It is also a normative sentence. "Complete" well-being is a standard almost no measured population meets all the time, so the sentence works as an aim of the organization, not as a diagnostic threshold a clinician can check off. This card quotes the constitution. It does not rank health systems.

contested_views.position: Health includes complete physical, mental, and social well-being, not only the absence of disease.
A definition that requires complete well-being is an aspiration rather than an operational diagnosis.
contested_views.held_by: A reading of the same sentence; this card does not cite a separate critic
